title: Generic Galois group of a finite local etale henselian residue lift
statement:
Let $(H,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] that is a normal domain (an integral domain integrally closed in its field of fractions) [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and put $K=\operatorname{Frac}(H)$. Let $B$ be a local finite etale $H$-algebra, meaning finite as an $H$-module with $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}H$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose an identification $B/\mathfrak mB\simeq e$ is given, where $e/\kappa$ is a finite Galois field extension [def-pc-field-extension], meaning finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and normal (every minimal polynomial over $\kappa$ of an element of $e$ splits in $e$). Then $B$ is a normal domain, $H\to B$ is injective, and $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B)=K\otimes_HB$ is a finite Galois extension of $K$ with $[E:K]=[e:\kappa]$. The ring $B$ is the integral closure of $H$ in $E$: it consists exactly of the elements of $E$ satisfying a monic polynomial over $H$. Extension to fractions and reduction give group isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Gal}(E/K)\simeq\operatorname{Aut}_H(B)\simeq\operatorname{Gal}(e/\kappa).$$
Here the first map restricts automorphisms to $B$, and the second is their action on $B/\mathfrak mB$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW (lemma-identify-inertia), proof paragraph beginning 'Let kappa prime/kappa be a finite Galois extension': the finite etale lift, its fraction fields and degrees, and the 'small detail omitted' calculation of the invariant ring. proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], every prime localization of the normal domain $H$ is a normal domain; hence $H$ is a normal ring in [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal] to $H\to B$ makes $B$ a normal ring. If $\mathfrak n$ is the unique maximal ideal of $B$, then $B=B_{\mathfrak n}$: every element outside $\mathfrak n$ is already a unit. The definition of a normal ring therefore says directly that $B$ is a normal domain. In particular it is integrally closed in $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$.

The etale map makes $B$ flat over $H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Since $H$ is local and $B$ is module-finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free] makes $B$ free. Choose a finite basis $b_1,\ldots,b_n$. Reducing its coordinate isomorphism $H^n\simeq B$ modulo $\mathfrak m$ gives $\kappa^n\simeq B/\mathfrak mB\simeq e$, so $n=[e:\kappa]>0$. If $h\in H$ maps to zero in $B$, it annihilates each $b_i$, whose coordinate vector has a coordinate equal to $1$; thus $h=0$. This proves injectivity and allows us to regard $H\subset B$ and $K\subset E$.

source.place: Tags 00U2 (lemma-etale), flatness clause, and 00NZ (lemma-finite-flat-local). The basis calculation supplies the degree calculation of Tag 0BSW.

proof.text: Inside $E$ put $C=\{b/s:b\in B,\ 0\ne s\in H\}$. The $b_i$ of step 2 form a $K$-basis of $C$: spanning follows by dividing their $H$-coordinate expansions by $s$, and independence follows by multiplying a putative $K$-linear relation by a common nonzero denominator in $H$ and using independence over $H$. For $0\ne c\in C$, multiplication by $c$ is an injective endomorphism of this $n$-dimensional $K$-vector space (since $C\subset E$); the images of a basis are $n$ independent vectors and hence a basis, so this map is surjective and $cd=1$ for some $d\in C$. Thus $C$ is a field containing $B$, and $C=E$. The map $K\otimes_HB\to C$, $k\otimes b\mapsto kb$, is an isomorphism: its inverse sends $b/s$ to $(1/s)\otimes b$. Equality of fractions implies equality after multiplying by the invertible scalar $s t$, and the tensor balancing relation checks both composites on pure tensors. Consequently $E=K\otimes_HB$ and $[E:K]=n=[e:\kappa]$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW (lemma-identify-inertia), fraction fields and degrees calculation; elementary basis and fraction calculation filling the omitted detail.

proof.text: Every $b\in B$ is integral over $H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Conversely let $x\in E$ satisfy a monic polynomial over $H$. The same polynomial, after the inclusion $H\subset B$, is monic over $B$. Since $B$ is a normal domain by step 1, [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] gives $x\in B$. Hence $B$ is exactly the integral closure of $H$ in $E$.

An $H$-algebra automorphism $\tau$ of $B$ extends uniquely to a $K$-automorphism of $E$ by $b/c\mapsto\tau(b)/\tau(c)$ for $c\ne0$ in $B$; the inverse is the analogous extension of $\tau^{-1}$. Conversely a $K$-automorphism $\sigma$ of $E$ sends a root of a monic $H$-polynomial to another root of the same polynomial, since it fixes $H\subset K$. Step 4 gives $\sigma(B)\subset B$, and applying it to $\sigma^{-1}$ gives equality. Restriction and extension are inverse by their formulas on $B$ and on fractions, and these formulas also preserve composition. We have proved $\operatorname{Aut}_K(E)\simeq\operatorname{Aut}_H(B)$ with restriction as the displayed forward map.

source.place: Tag 0BSW (lemma-identify-inertia), passage to fraction fields; explicit elementary automorphism calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-map-bijective] with $R=H$ and $S=T=B$. Its hypotheses hold because $H$ is henselian local and $B$ is finite etale. It identifies $\operatorname{End}_H(B)$ with $\operatorname{End}_\kappa(e)$ by reduction. Reduction respects identity and composition. For any $\kappa$-automorphism $u$ of $e$, lift both $u$ and $u^{-1}$ using surjectivity; their two composites reduce to the identity and so are identities by injectivity. Thus these lifts are inverse automorphisms. Conversely the reduction of an automorphism has the reduced inverse. Restricting the bijection therefore gives $\operatorname{Aut}_H(B)\simeq\operatorname{Gal}(e/\kappa)$, with the prescribed action on $B/\mathfrak mB$.

source.place: Tag 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale), full faithfulness, applied to automorphisms by lifting inverses.

proof.text: Let $G=\operatorname{Aut}_H(B)$, acting on $E$ by step 5. The action is faithful, since its restriction to $B$ is the original automorphism. By step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-fixed-field] applied to the given finite Galois extension $e/\kappa$, $G$ is finite and $|G|=[e:\kappa]=n$. Set $F=E^G$; it contains $K$ because every extended automorphism fixes $K$. The new general field-action leaf [lem-wf-finite-field-action-fixed-degree] gives that $E/F$ is finite Galois and $[E:F]=|G|=n$. Also $F/K$ is finite: a $K$-linearly independent subset of $F$ remains independent in the finite-dimensional space $E$, so its size is at most $n$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] gives $n=[E:K]=[E:F][F:K]=n[F:K]$. Since $n>0$, $[F:K]=1$. The nonzero element $1$ is consequently a $K$-basis of $F$, giving $F=K$. Hence $E/K$ is Galois. Combining steps 5 and 6 yields exactly the two displayed group isomorphisms and their stated maps.
